title: Hunter Serotonin Toxicity Criteria
sources: Dunkley EJC et al. QJM 2003 (Hunter Area Toxicology Service criteria)
purpose: Diagnoses serotonin toxicity in a patient who has taken a serotonergic agent. More sensitive (84%) and specific (97%) than the older Sternbach criteria. The rule is a set of decision paths — ANY one path being satisfied makes the diagnosis; the point tally here is a helper.

items.label: Inducible clonus PLUS agitation or diaphoresis
Ocular clonus PLUS agitation or diaphoresis
Hypertonia PLUS temperature > 38 °C PLUS (ocular clonus OR inducible clonus)

interpretation.label: No Hunter pathway satisfied — serotonin toxicity not diagnosed by these criteria. Reconsider anticholinergic toxidrome, NMS (bradyreflexia, lead-pipe rigidity, days-long onset), sympathomimetic toxicity, meningitis

At least one Hunter pathway satisfied — SEROTONIN TOXICITY. Stop all serotonergic agents; benzodiazepines for agitation / tremor / mild hyperthermia; aggressive cooling and paralysis + intubation if temp > 38.5–39 °C; cyproheptadine 12 mg then 2 mg q2h (or 4–8 mg q6h) for moderate–severe cases; avoid physical restraints (worsen hyperthermia / lactic acidosis)

notes: Onset is usually within 6–24 h of a dose change or an added agent (MAOI + SSRI, linezolid, methylene blue, tramadol, fentanyl, triptans, dextromethorphan, MDMA). Clonus and hyperreflexia are typically lower-limb predominant. Severe features: temp > 41.1 °C, rigidity, rising CK/creatinine, DIC — treat as a hyperthermic emergency.
buildNote: Decision-rule helper — each row is a complete Hunter pathway; any one → diagnosis.
